name: Gulf / US–Iran war
value: LNG tanker hit mine 13 Nov; 10 ships hit in Nov
summary: Iran's IRGC says a gas tanker hit a mine in Hormuz on 13 Nov; at least 10 ships were hit in the first 10 days of Nov
state: Iran's Revolutionary Guards navy said a tanker carrying gas struck a mine and exploded in the Strait of Hormuz on 13 Nov while using what it called an unauthorised route, a day after it said four oil tankers were hit by explosions (Reuters via gCaptain). The Washington Institute counts at least 10 ships hit in the first 10 days of November after 37 attacks in October. The IRGC also said on 13 Nov it destroyed a US radar in Bahrain after a US strike in Sirik, Iran (AP via Just Security). Attacks on Gulf shipping and state-on-state strikes set the Alert.
for_you: Seafarers and shipping firms should follow UKMTO guidance for the Gulf and Strait of Hormuz; travellers in the region should check FCDO advice. Attacks on tankers tend to lift oil, gas and freight costs and insurance premiums.
rubric_hit: Alert: attacks on Gulf shipping — gas tanker hit by mine 13 Nov, at least 10 ships hit 1–10 Nov

why: Direct hostilities between Iran and the US or Israel threaten Gulf energy infrastructure, the Strait of Hormuz and the wider region.
drivers: Strikes and retaliation, attacks on shipping and Gulf states, mediation and ceasefire talks, US force posture.

rubric.alert: Active strikes between states, attacks on Gulf energy infrastructure or shipping, or the Strait of Hormuz substantially closed.
rubric.watch: A ceasefire or stalemate with sporadic strikes, or credible threats of renewed strikes.
rubric.normal: No direct state-on-state hostilities; diplomacy active.
